answer: An admission auction stops bulk forgery: only 200 slots open each epoch, and each applicant bids twice its 30-day earnings, locked for 20 epochs. A pigment trader bidding for one slot pays once, but a forger must outbid honest agents slot by slot, since every copy needs its own deposit. A grove keeper forging 100 identities thus pays 6,000 days of income. A walnut seller playing honestly recovers its bid in 6 epochs and keeps undiluted rewards.
